content:
Let the area be \(K\). Then the side lengths are

\[
a=\frac{2K}{4}=\frac K2,\qquad b=\frac{2K}{12}=\frac K6,\qquad c=\frac{2K}{x}.
\]

Triangle inequalities give:

\[
a+b>c \implies \frac K2+\frac K6>\frac{2K}{x} \implies x>3,
\]

\[
b+c>a \implies \frac K6+\frac{2K}{x}>\frac K2 \implies x<6.
\]

So the integer height \(x\) satisfies

\[
3<x<6,
\]

so \(x=4\) or \(x=5\). The longest possible height is

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
